permutationLabel: Amoebic (Caribbean context) — serology positive, single homogeneous right-lobe abscess
summary: 32-year-old man from rural Saint Lucia with 2 weeks of fever and RUQ pain after dysentery a month ago; T 38.6 °C; WBC 15.8, ALP 210; E. histolytica serology positive; ultrasound: single 6 cm homogeneous hypoechoic lesion in segment VIII.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Fever and right upper abdominal pain for two weeks
inputs.hpi: Two weeks of fever and right upper quadrant pain worse on breathing and lying on the right side. Bloody diarrhoea for a week about a month ago, settled without treatment. Lives in a rural community with a shared water supply. No jaundice.

exam.abdomen: Tender hepatomegaly with point tenderness over the right lower intercostal spaces. No peritonism.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Single 6 × 5 cm round, homogeneous, hypoechoic subcapsular lesion in segment VIII of the right lobe with fine internal echoes and no septa — appearances of an amoebic abscess. No duct dilatation. Gallbladder normal.

inputs.socialHistory: Banana farmer, rural Saint Lucia. Alcohol occasionally.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Amoebic liver abscess
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Amoebic liver abscess (E. histolytica serology positive), single 6 cm abscess in segment VIII. No rupture.

mustInclude.note: Amoebicidal metronidazole (e.g. 750–800 mg TDS). A generic anaerobic-cover metronidazole in a sepsis or peritonism bundle does not count.
mustInclude.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine management index: map A06.4 to the liver_abscess protocol (amoebic branch: metronidazole 750–800 mg TDS 7–10 days then a luminal agent) and see mgmt-no-appendicectomy.

mustInclude.note: A luminal amoebicide after metronidazole prevents relapse and onward transmission.
mustInclude.proposedFix: liver_abscess protocol: add paromomycin or diloxanide furoate after metronidazole for amoebic abscess.

mustExclude.note: Uncomplicated amoebic abscess responds to metronidazole; aspiration is for non-response at 3–5 days, left-lobe abscess or imminent rupture.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden management item present in ios.radiation.plan: "pyogenic: iv antibiotics (biliary/enteric cover) + percutaneous drainage of large abscesses; find the source (biliary, colonic)"

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.proposedFix: AssessmentTab ManagementPanel: when the clinician has confirmed/locked a working diagnosis (ICD or disease id), show that protocol instead of the PANE top (≥0.20). Today a confirmed pancreatitis/amoebic abscess shows the cholecystitis or appendicitis protocol.

guideline.name: Amebiasis (narrative review — no formal international guideline exists)
guideline.section: Amoebic liver abscess: serology; metronidazole (or tinidazole) followed by a luminal agent (paromomycin, diloxanide furoate) to eradicate intestinal carriage; aspiration only for no response, left-lobe or imminent rupture
guideline.citation: Haque R, Huston CD, Hughes M, Houpt E, Petri WA Jr. N Engl J Med. 2003;348:1565–1573.

guideline.name: Hepatic abscess: diagnosis and management (narrative review — no formal international guideline exists)
guideline.section: Pyogenic abscess: blood cultures, CT, antibiotics for 4–6 weeks, percutaneous drainage/aspiration for larger abscesses, look for a biliary or colonic source; multiple cholangitic abscesses: treat the biliary obstruction
guideline.citation: Lardière-Deguelte S, Ragot E, Amroun K, et al. J Visc Surg. 2015;152:231–243.

rationale: Permutation: amoebic abscess, relevant to the Caribbean setting. The distinguishing guideline actions are metronidazole followed by a luminal agent, with drainage reserved for non-response or high-risk location.
